column2: Youth will track their spending for four weeks and identify one change to their habits.
Participants will understand the difference between a debit card and a credit card and the cost of interest.
Teens earning summer wages will deposit at least 25% of each paycheck into a savings account.
Students will be able to read a pay stub and explain payroll deductions.
Youth aging out of foster care will have at least one permanent, caring adult connection by age 21.
Transition-age youth will obtain their birth certificate, Social Security card, and state ID before exiting care.
Youth in extended foster care will enroll in health insurance through Medicaid until age 26.
Young adults will maintain their own apartment lease for 12 consecutive months.
Youth will demonstrate independent living skills such as cooking, budgeting, and scheduling appointments.
Youth staying at the shelter will exit to a safe and stable housing situation.
Runaway youth will be reunified with family when it is safe to do so.
Youth experiencing homelessness will reduce nights spent on the street or in unsafe locations.
Teen parents will stay enrolled in high school through the birth of their child.
Young mothers will complete all recommended well-child visits for their infant.
Teen parents will delay a second pregnancy for at least 24 months.
LGBTQ+ youth will report feeling safe and affirmed in program spaces.
Youth will report greater self-acceptance of their sexual orientation and gender identity.
LGBTQ+ youth will report fewer experiences of harassment at school after the GSA launch.
Campers will demonstrate increased independence in self-care tasks away from home.
4-H members will demonstrate public speaking skills by giving a demonstration at the county fair.
Scouts will learn wilderness first aid and outdoor safety skills.
Campers will try an activity that initially made them nervous, such as swimming in the lake.
Youth will get at least eight hours of sleep on school nights.
Participants will complete an annual dental and vision screening.
Students with asthma will reduce emergency room visits through improved self-management.
Youth will be able to name three methods of preventing sexually transmitted infections.
Students will increase daily consumption of fruits and vegetables.
Sites will improve their Youth Program Quality Assessment scores in the interaction and engagement domains.
The organization will achieve accreditation from the state afterschool network.
Staff turnover will decrease to below 20% annually.
The coalition will establish a shared data system across five youth-serving agencies.
The school district will adopt a policy guaranteeing afterschool transportation for all students.
Neighborhood residents will report increased trust in one another and willingness to intervene for youth safety.
The city will allocate dedicated funding for summer youth employment in the annual budget.
Students with IEPs will lead their own IEP meetings by the end of the school year.
The program will provide accommodations (sensory kits, visual schedules) so all youth can participate.
Youth with disabilities will transition into competitive integrated employment after high school.
Parents with limited English proficiency will receive school communications in their home language.
Newcomer families will understand their rights regarding school enrollment regardless of immigration status.
Refugee youth will maintain fluency in their home language while learning English.
Youth will take action to reduce waste at home, such as recycling and composting.
Participants will report feeling calmer and more restored after time spent in nature.
Players will improve their dribbling, passing, and shooting skills.
Athletes will maintain passing grades to remain eligible for the team.
Children will develop fundamental movement skills such as running, jumping, throwing, and catching.
Girls in the program will increasingly see themselves as 'a STEM person.'
Students will apply the engineering design process to build and test a prototype.
Participants will enroll in an advanced STEM course the following school year.
Youth will evaluate the credibility of online news sources and identify misinformation.
Student reporters will publish at least two articles in the community newspaper.
Youth will improve their persuasive writing skills.
First-generation students will persist into their second year of college.
Students will visit at least three college campuses before senior year.
Seniors will be able to compare financial aid award letters and calculate net cost.
Alumni will complete a bachelor's degree within six years.
Summer youth employees will receive a positive supervisor evaluation.
Apprentices will complete a registered apprenticeship program.
Program graduates will be employed or in education six months after exit.
Youth will be able to identify warning signs of dating violence.
Participants will report carrying a weapon less often.
Outreach workers will mediate conflicts to prevent retaliatory shootings in the neighborhood.
Students will participate in restorative circles to repair harm instead of receiving a suspension.
Out-of-school suspensions will decrease by 30% at partner schools.
Youth diverted from court will complete their restorative agreement.
Youth will report lower intentions to vape in the next year.
Students will perceive greater risk of harm from regular marijuana use.
Mentees will expand their professional network by connecting with at least three adults in careers of interest.
Mentors will complete 6 hours of pre-match training.
Mentees will report that their mentor challenges them to keep improving.
Children will demonstrate fine motor skills such as holding a pencil and using scissors.
Children will show persistence and curiosity when working on puzzles and new tasks.
Infants and toddlers will receive developmental screenings and referrals as needed.
Home visitors will observe increased positive parent-child interactions.
Parents will complete their GED or enroll in job training.
Caregivers will build friendships with other parents in the program.
Parents will report knowing where to turn for help in a crisis.
Parents will serve on the program's family advisory council.
Students will report that there is an adult at the program who notices when they are absent.
Youth will choose to return to the program for a second year.
Students will say they feel proud to be part of the program.
Youth will practice gratitude by writing thank-you notes to community volunteers.
Students will report higher life satisfaction and a sense of flourishing.
School counselors will implement a universal SEL screener.
Students who experienced trauma will report feeling safe at school.
Students will be able to name three trusted adults or resources they can contact in a mental health crisis.
Third graders will read on grade level by the end of the year.
Ninth graders will earn enough credits to be promoted to tenth grade.
Students will believe that their intelligence can grow with effort.
Students will ask questions in class and participate in discussions.
Students will score proficient on the state science assessment.
Youth will explain how a bill becomes a law in their state.
Youth will stand up for classmates who are being treated unfairly.
Youth council members will co-design program activities with staff.
Students will critique a peer's artwork using the language of the discipline.
Youth will compose an original song.
Students will connect a historical artwork to their own cultural experience.
Youth will practice forgiveness in their relationships with family and friends.
Youth will secure a job within 90 days of release.
Youth will avoid a new adjudication while on probation.
Students will earn college credit through dual enrollment in a CTE pathway.
Youth will demonstrate safe use of tools in the construction trades lab.
Program staff will collect pre- and post-surveys from all participants.
Participants will benefit from high-quality programming.
